dimensions.assessment: Neither token is merely a synopsis. The shorter token keeps causally productive turns: wet ink obstructs moving the loan slip, lunch requires repacking, the wrong bundle prompts actual unpacking, dispatch and inspection, and withdrawal changes who writes and buys. The longer token gains a second face-to-face visit and a longer relationship, but repeated tea, paper and guest-talk loops sometimes restate a point already made. This dimension favors the shorter token for specific causal density, not shortness itself.

The longer token gives the two Baoyus reciprocal wit: the guest offers to witness a conversation he could not hear, the host plays back his book-return joke, and 麝月 treats a name as a free resource. The shorter token's same-name/tea joke is economical and work-connected, but a messenger returning the jade loses the second in-person round and some of Zhen Baoyu's sociability. Extra length earns its place here because of a particular added relationship, not by default.

The longer token distinguishes wrapping colors, seals, addressees and worn cord-hole marks, and the hosts do not read the letters. However its lifting-both/letter-bundle-left inconsistency breaks the displayed exchange. The shorter token distinguishes the missing home loose-leaf booklet from the guest's worm-eaten volume, reconstructs custody with the servant, limits the deliverer's knowledge to his commission, and checks booklet, cloth and jade on receipt. A sender's note remains a claim until unpacking confirms those contents; neither spoken ownership nor a note is external provenance proof.

The longer token's 麝月 barbs, Zhen Baoyu's light evasions and Baochai's spending decisions are distinguishable; the grief pause interrupts book talk rather than becoming an exposition speech. The shorter token gives Baochai sharper practical boundaries, Jia Yun verification questions, 麝月 blunt care and Zhen Baoyu responsibility rather than blame. Both sometimes give several people similarly polished object-jokes, so wit alone is not proof of individual voices. The shorter token joins talk more closely to hands and bowls; the longer token develops the visitor's voice more expansively.

The longer token lets Baochai fear illness/lodging, 麝月 wait, and Baoyu admit leaving is wrong; no monk supplies a revelation excusing him. The shorter token more sharply separates refusing to live at home from lacking an itinerary. 麝月 will not use feeding as a bribe; Baochai pulls the unfinished garment away from his reaching hand and asserts her own decision. It loses some repeated days of worried waiting but gains a clear, morally costly refusal without a narrator declaring enlightenment.

The longer token's son retaining the worn sleeve and the gradual conversion of an empty room to ordinary storage give bereavement a longer material aftermath. Clothes and an unchanged old box outlast congratulations. The shorter token compresses that duration but has the son accidentally ask whether his dead mother's meal has been delivered, then still eat and answer funeral work. Its old robe is familiar to a hand, not only an economy symbol. Accretive aftermath and concentrated habit-error are different gains; neither cancels the other.

Both make tea, rice, repairs, medicine and borrowed furniture constrain behavior. The longer token's tea decision and pharmacy debt avoid effortless abundance. The shorter token also reserves rent money, reimburses Jia Yun's search rather than treating his labor as free, distinguishes future salary from present bills, and notices that non-cash funeral gifts do not pay a deposit. Medical watching requires another person to watch food. Compression retains choices and labor rather than merely listing poverty props.

The longer token explicitly places several years before examination success and further years before actual appointment, making the distinction hard to miss. The shorter token gives several winters/summers through changing hems, book threads, window patches and repeated waiting for a vacancy: its elapsed time is enacted and not absent. It compresses the exam-stage/appointment distinction more. The longer token is more legible on that specific dimension; the shorter token gains lived waiting instead of a bare date jump.

The longer token rejects an expensive gift precisely because an office now exists, keeps the old box and borrowed furniture, and fixes a roof rather than buying a facade. The shorter token lets a child ask why money has not reached the cooking pot and explicitly says old house and property have not returned. Appointment and honor do not automatically repair finances. Both show real financial limits; neither scene authenticates a historical office, legal restoration rule or unseen plot constraint.

The longer token supplies a heavy coronet, two pressure marks, airing and storage in the unchanged old box. The shorter token enacts repeated fitting, tightness, standing fatigue and the known sleeve of the old robe after removal. The former gains the ceremonial object's longer afterlife; the latter tactile familiarity and the son's participation. Neither turns Li Wan into only an emblem of glory. Neither independently proves the rank or costume specification.

No source card or external calendar is exposed. The longer token starts a final conversation at winter's end, then says several days pass before terminal decline; death occurs toward late afternoon with no numbered month. The shorter token explicitly puts death several months after honor and enacts reduced eating, drinking and waking, but gives no named death month. Both establish elapsed months/nursing, not an externally required exact month. Missing external verification is not converted into FAIL.

The longer token recognizes the returned jade by cord-hole abrasion; the guest's claim to have barely looked is not external authentication. The shorter token follows the packed object, disallows wiping it, dispatches a messenger, and recognizes the still-snagging cord on receipt. Both show actual jade in chapter 98 rather than a metaphysical label. The longer token's local packet-chain FAIL is separately retained. Neither departure tracks continued jade wearing, and neither shows jade materially changing into the mountain stone. Such missing custody/transport remains unverified; no route is invented.

The longer token keeps false east/north/ferry reports distinct from the later message; its unnamed temple lies beyond two village roads by a pine grove, and Jia Yun misses a fork. The novice admits not knowing the first days. The shorter token keeps incompatible cart reports apart, declines a hearsay river crossing, and asks several unnamed temples before direct recognition. Both show Baoyu working at a temple. Neither verifies a named real temple, precise city, first itinerary or transport constraint. Searcher travel is not Baoyu's route, and an unshown route is not a verified contradictory route or a FAIL.

The longer token leaves Baochai with a rough thread and unfinished shoulder seam, not immediately rethreading, while boiling water grows audible: a stopped hand holds absence. The shorter token gives 麝月 an old eye plugged by broken thread, a new needle only half threaded, interruption by the fire, and the question of whom the garment is for. It ends by moving the unfinished sleeve away from soup while two women eat. Bodily continuation and a sparer suspended gesture are distinct effects. Neither completes the garment to manufacture emotional closure.

Both expose 正、副、再副、三副、四副. The principal layer has the same twelve women, with a different initial order and 巧姐 versus 贾巧姐. 香菱 is visible in 副, 晴雯 and 袭人 in 再副. Only 黛玉's 情情 and the final Baoyu 情不情 are supplied as ratings. The longer token says the deepest layers hold denser names without reading them aloud. The shorter token labels five layers of names but says no writing is visible on the 三副/四副 remaining paper, reducing their populatedness on-page. This is a visibility weakness, not a proven contradiction: 未见 need not mean nonexistent. No unseen complete roster/rating rule is authenticated.

The longer token closes human affairs, opens a timeless 太虚 sequence, closes the thin-fate doors, then moves to 大荒山无稽崖青埂峰 before the copyist. The shorter token also closes human affairs, leaves 太虚 undated, and explicitly sets that realm aside before 青埂峰. Neither gives the humans a dream explanation excusing Baoyu's refusal or Li Wan's death, nor lets the roster rewrite household choices. The short transition preserves boundaries; the longer version gives fuller thresholds. Both copyists leave illegibility blank rather than manufacture text.

The longer token explicitly states restored original stone form and return to the old place, then distinguishes a later visitor and copying. The shorter token's chapter title claims 石归山 but the body begins with a visitor finding a stone still inscribed; it stages copying, not the return event. Compression gains economy and a careful copyist but loses the event and full mountain-location wording. This shown-versus-claimed narrational gap is not authentication of mythic geography or proof of an external constraint violation, and it does not supply an unseen physical jade transport chain.

The public packet supplies two candidate sequences and byte bindings only: no source card, earlier chapters, complete novel, canonical route, historical appointment data, exact required death month or complete roster. Neither token can be authenticated against such absent material. Recognizing character names and familiar frame motifs is a possible learned-model bias, not evidence that either token is canonical or training-known.
